pr_title: Allow selection of statistics state characteristic
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Hey there, happy to contribute my first piece of code to home-assistant/core 🙂 Please do not hold back with remarks.

The [statistics integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/statistics/) takes a sensor and generates stats for a number of its historic state changes. The resulting new sensor has the mean as its state and a bunch of useful statistical measures as attributes.

This PR adds the ability to name the main statistical measure to be accessible right through the sensor state, instead of "mean". This makes a lot of use cases of the statistics integration a lot easier to employ for users.

All changes are non-breaking, even though that would have been easier 😉

Btw. this integration doesn't have any type annotations or tests. Please let me know if you need that added as part of this PR. I intend to add further measures and a breaking change to the configuration in a future PR. **Edit:**  Regarding tests I found https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/40896 and would be happy to pick this up next

Personal note, in a future PR I want to contribute:


Configuration:
  - number of measurements AND/OR age (most of the time only one or the other is needed)
  - compute_all - True default, If False, no attributes will be added
  - percentile/quantile for state value
  - source entity attribute as source measurement
  - more attributes for binary_sensor
  - Add unique_id
 
Attributes:
  - Context:
    - buffer_ratio (percentage of limit used by samples)
  - Main statistics (for the average user, aimed at direct use cases):
    - count
    - age_range (timedelta)
    - sum
    - difference_first_last (simply "difference" for now)
    - difference_min_max (current "change")
    - noisiness (simple version of a noise ratio. Sum of all differences, divided by samples)
    - min_value
    - max_value
  - Detailed statistics (for the data nerds among us):
    - mean
    - median
    - standard deviation
    - variance
    - quartile_1
    - quartile_3
    - percentile_breadth_5-95 (? can be derived from stddev)
    - percentile_breadth_1-99 (? can be derived from stddev)
    - quantiles (incl. dynamic number of cutpoints)

Home Assistant 2021.9.7

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

### Link to integration documentation on our website

_No response_

```yaml
sensor:
  - platform: statistics
    entity_id:

    name: For more detail please enter

    precision: 0
```

Hello @behnam85, I was able to confirm this behavior but statistics immediately recalculated when the next source sensor value arrived. Do you see the short "Unknown" time as a bug?

Hey @emontnemery some quick advice? Sounds like `async_update` is not called as part of the reload of the statistics sensor - or it is called too early and looses the race to the recorder loading.
I'll work on a PR ;) Thanks

review_comments: I brought this into a helper function and tidied up the logic as was meaningful. All related testcases remain green.
How come we don't need the try/except anymore?

Because the only reason these will throw `StatisticsError` (instead of ValueError or TypeError) is when there are not enough samples in the buffer. I've made this implicit condition explicit, which makes the whole function cleaner and less nested.
@emontnemery you were the one to move the this into `_add_state_to_queue` in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/58023. Is deriving the unit upon every new state value really necessary?

There's no guarantee the source sensor did not change its unit.
We can decorate `_derive_unit_of_measurement` with `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)` to avoid recalculating.
Nice. I can still learn some things from you :)

I gave this a shot but as far as I got, my conclusion is that I would need to convert the function into a staticmethod. Not a total showstopper but feels like it's not worth it for this arguably low-complexity function. Will leave as is.

Yes, you're absolutely right about that.
We would have to use some 3rd party library to have it work as expected.
Goes hand in hand with the introduction of configurable state characteristic
